Find the values of $x$ for which the function $g(x)=\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{7}{4}{x}^{2}+\frac{3}{2}x+1$ is strictly increasing.

feedback.worked_solution:
The function is strictly increasing where ${g}^{′}(x)>0.$ Differentiating $g(x),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & ={x}^{2}-\frac{7}{2}x+\frac{3}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

so we need to solve the inequality

$$
{x}^{2}-\frac{7}{2}x+\frac{3}{2}>0.
$$

The above inequality factors as

$$
(x-\frac{1}{2})(x-3)>0.
$$

The graph of $y=(x-\frac{1}{2})(x-3)$ has roots at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and $x=3,$ as shown below:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14014428/assets/26374f7e5c86c5585d384b3e65b4a1b3fb2f94172ed753cdb3fe7bdb0af0abb8.png)

For an upward-opening parabola, the product $(x-\frac{1}{2})(x-3)$ is positive when $x<\frac{1}{2}$ or $x>3.$

Therefore, we conclude that the function is strictly increasing on the intervals 

$$
x<\frac{1}{2}\,\text{and}\,x>3.
$$
